 Vadodara Municipal Corporation Meeting | Bhukhi Kans Rerouting Work Approved
 3 of 22 works postponed at Standing Committee meeting: Final meeting held before Diwali; no fresh tender for Bhukhi Kans re-routing work
 Vadodara 3 hours ago 
 Copy link 
 Vadodara Municipal Corporation's final Standing Committee meeting before Diwali was held. The meeting discussed a total of 22 items placed on the agenda, of which three were deferred, one was approved with changes and the remaining items were approved. In particular, approval was given to entrust the work of rerouting the Bhukhi Kans, aimed at rescuing Wards 1 and 2 from flooding, to the old contractor.
 Two stormwater drain extension works deferred Extension works for stormwater drains in all four zones had been placed before the Standing Committee. A proposal had been submitted to increase the financial limit for a ₹50 lakh project to ₹80 lakh, while two of the four works were rejected. The works to be carried out in the South Zone were deferred. In addition, the other stormwater drain works were approved. One additional work had also been included in the agenda, and it too was approved.
 Providing a 5.36% GST adjustment will increase the corporation's burden According to a circular issued by the Gujarat government's Roads and Buildings Department, the implementation of tax reimbursement as per GST bills will affect the financial structure of various aspects of the tender process and the related procedures.
 In view of the change in the GST slab rate, contractors will be compensated by 5.36%, following the method adopted by the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation and the Director General (CPWD) for GST-related matters.
 The municipal corporation will have to reimburse this amount to contractors who claim it. However, the proposal is expected to increase the burden on the civic body by approximately ₹100 crore. The Standing Committee has also approved this work.
 Re-tender Not Conducted for Re-routing Work Under this much-discussed project for sewage and stormwater disposal in the city, works from Chhani Jakatnaka to Nizampura Muktidham (Phase-2) and from the canal to Chhani Jakatnaka (Phase-1) had earlier been approved.
 However, due to the displeasure and opposition of local residents, it has become difficult to proceed with both projects at their originally designated locations, prompting the authorities to consider a new option involving a change of location.
 The Standing Committee had approved the Phase-2 work for M/s Shivalay Infra Project Pvt Ltd at a bid price 2.39% below the estimated cost of ₹21.66 crore, namely ₹21,14,99,749 plus GST.
 Phase 1 of the work was awarded to M/s Rajkamal Builders Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. at a rate 1.5% below the estimated amount of ₹18.63 crore, for ₹18,35,23,655 plus GST.
 A proposal to re-route the water channel has been put forward. Under the proposal, it was suggested that the Bhukhi Kans, which enters the city parallel to National Highway 48, be trapped at a suitable location and that a new stormwater channel be constructed along the 12-metre-wide road on the city side. The proposal has been approved.
 New work will increase expenditure by ₹17 crore The work to re-route the Bhukhi Kans was earlier approved at ₹35 crore. However, as the route has now been extended, the same work is likely to cost ₹52 crore if carried out at the old rates.
 Considering public sentiment and the prevailing circumstances, carrying out the work at the designated locations appears impractical at first glance. The authorities have now put forward a new option as a practical solution to the problem.
